# Bio-NICE Two-Model System: Evaluation Report

**System:** Model 1 (relevance gate) → Model 2 (AI-integration level classifier)
**Prepared from:** `outputs/model1_relevance_*.csv`, `outputs/model2_ai_integration_*.csv` (repository outputs, generated by `src/train_relevance_model.py` and `src/train_ai_integration_model.py`)

---

## 1. Purpose and system design

The Bio-NICE prediction system classifies biotech/pharma job postings in two sequential stages:

**Stage 1 — Model 1, the relevance gate.** A TF-IDF + Logistic Regression classifier assigns every posting one of four relevance labels: **Core**, **Adjacent**, **Company-context only**, or **Exclude**. If Model 1 predicts **Exclude**, the posting is treated as outside the Bio-NICE domain entirely (e.g., an unrelated job title), and the pipeline stops there — no AI-integration score is produced, because a confident-but-meaningless score on an out-of-scope posting is worse than no score at all.

**Stage 2 — Model 2, the AI-integration classifier.** For any posting Model 1 did **not** call Exclude, a second TF-IDF (+ structured term-count features) + Logistic Regression classifier predicts the degree of AI/data integration in the role: **None**, **Low**, **Moderate**, or (in principle) **High**. Postings labeled "Company-context only" by Model 1 (e.g., an HR or Sales role at a real biotech company) are deliberately still passed through Model 2, which maps them to "None" — a true, useful answer, not a meaningless one.

Both models share the same input text construction: `title | description`, whitespace-normalized. Model 1 uses TF-IDF only; Model 2 additionally uses six structured term-hit-count features (AI/ML term count, data-science term count, computational-biology term count, biotech-domain term count, tools/frameworks term count, and their total).

---

## 2. Dataset

### 2.1 Size and provenance

- **Source pool:** `biotech_postings_4857_classified.csv` — 4,857 biotech/pharma-relevant postings pulled from the full raw LinkedIn Job Postings 2023–2024 archive (123,849 unique postings, all dated Dec 2023–Apr 2024), filtered by LinkedIn industry code or a biotech/pharma keyword regex (see `README_biotech_postings_4857.md`). This pool is rule-filtered, not hand-labeled.
- **Labeling:** All 4,857 postings were split into 122 batches of up to 40 postings each (`src/03_prepare_ai_labeling_batches.py`), labeled by an AI agent loop (`ai_manual_label`, `ai_bionice_role`, `ai_confidence`), merged (`src/04_merge_ai_labeled_batches.py`), and passed through a rule-based QC correction pass (`src/05_clean_agent_loop_labels.py`) that reclassifies any "Core" posting whose title matches business/admin or patient-care/service false-positive terms *and* lacks strong Core evidence terms (bioinformatics, data scientist, machine learning, biostatistics, etc.).
- **Labeling completeness: the full pool, not a partial sample.** All 4,857 postings carry a valid `agent_loop_clean_label` in the final training file (`data/processed/linkedin_v2_ai_labeled_broad_biotech_pool_agent_loop_cleaned_v1.csv`) — **4,857 of 4,857**. Both training scripts support a "high-confidence-only" filter that would exclude postings flagged for human review, but the review-flag column (`agent_loop_needs_human_review`) does not exist in this dataset, so the filter is a no-op here: every model result below reflects all 4,857 postings, not a QA-filtered subset.
- **QC correction had zero effect on this run.** Re-running the QC correction logic against the merged file shows 0 postings were reclassified by the business-false-positive rule and 0 by the patient-care/exclude-false-positive rule — the pre-QC and post-QC label distributions are identical (210 / 2,047 / 1,696 / 904 for Core / Adjacent / Company-context only / Exclude). The rubric ran as designed; it simply found no violations to correct in this labeling pass.
- **Label confidence caveat:** `ai_confidence` takes only two distinct values across the dataset — 0.70 (2,555 postings) and 0.85 (2,301 postings), plus a single 0.75 — consistent with a template-level confidence tag from the labeling agent rather than a per-posting calibrated estimate. Labels are AI-agent-assigned with rule-based QC, not independently human-adjudicated ground truth.

### 2.2 The corrected Bio-NICE relevance rubric

- **Core:** explicit job-level evidence of data science, AI/ML, computational biology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, statistical programming, clinical data management, RWE/HEOR, QSP/pharmacometrics, computational chemistry, or omics/biomarker analytics.
- **Adjacent:** life-science/biomedical roles without strong AI/data/computational evidence — wet-lab research, QA/GxP, biomanufacturing, clinical operations, regulatory, field application roles.
- **Company-context only:** business, sales, finance, HR, legal, marketing, commercial, or generic operations roles at a relevant biotech/pharma/healthcare/AI company.
- **Exclude:** out-of-scope patient-care, technician, service, warehouse, retail, maintenance, or otherwise unrelated postings.

The "corrected" part of the rubric is the post-hoc QC pass described above: any AI-agent-assigned "Core" label on a posting whose title matches business/admin or patient-care/service terms, and that lacks explicit Core evidence, is downgraded to "Company-context only" or "Exclude" respectively. As noted, this pass changed 0 labels in the current dataset.

### 2.3 Class distribution

**Model 1 target (relevance label), n = 4,857:**

| Label | Count | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Adjacent | 2,047 | 42.1% |
| Company-context only | 1,696 | 34.9% |
| Exclude | 904 | 18.6% |
| Core | 210 | 4.3% |

**Model 2 target (AI-integration level), n = 4,857:**

| Level | Count | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| None | 2,600 | 53.5% |
| Low | 2,047 | 42.1% |
| Moderate | 210 | 4.3% |
| High | 0 | 0.0% |

Note the exact correspondence: None = Exclude ∪ Company-context only (904 + 1,696 = 2,600); Low = Adjacent (2,047); Moderate = Core (210). See §4.2 and §6 for why this correspondence is deterministic, not a modeling result.

### 3.4 What the Exclude-class numbers mean in practice

Exclude precision is 0.7965 and recall is 0.8009 (F1 = 0.7987, on 904 held-out postings). In practice:

- **Recall 0.80** means that of the 904 genuinely out-of-scope postings, the gate correctly identifies and stops ~80% (724/904) before they ever reach Model 2. The remaining ~20% (180 postings: 4 misrouted as Core, 87 as Adjacent, 89 as Company-context only) leak through the gate and get an AI-integration score anyway — a score that is not meaningful for an out-of-scope posting.
- **Precision 0.7965** means that of everything the gate flags as Exclude (909 predictions: 724 correct + 89 + 87 + 4... — computed from the confusion matrix column, 724/(724+144+41+4)=0.7965), about 20% are actually relevant postings (mostly true Adjacent roles, 144 of them) that get wrongly rejected and never scored at all, even though they belong in the pipeline.
- Net effect: the gate is a reasonably effective filter but not a precise one. False negatives (Exclude postings that slip through) are the more consequential failure mode given the system's design rationale (an out-of-scope score is "worse than no score"); this model lets roughly 1 in 5 truly out-of-scope postings through.
- Core is the weakest class by a wide margin (F1 0.6502, on only 210 examples) — the smallest class, and also the class most often confused with Company-context only (42 of 210 Core postings misrouted there) and Adjacent (23 misrouted there). This is consistent with Core being the rarest and most semantically overlapping category (roles with genuine computational/AI substance embedded in otherwise ordinary-sounding biotech titles).

## 4. Model 2 results — AI-integration level classifier

Source: `outputs/model2_ai_integration_classification_report.csv`, `outputs/model2_ai_integration_confusion_matrix.csv`, `outputs/model2_ai_integration_cv_results.csv`. These reflect the Logistic Regression variant (the same model whose coefficients are reported in §5); a Random Forest variant was also trained and is available separately (`*_rf.csv` outputs) with comparable but not identical performance (mean F1-macro 0.6216 vs. 0.6249 for logistic regression across the 5 folds) — not reported in detail here since it was not requested.

### 4.3 Cross-validation, per fold

| Fold | F1-macro | F1-weighted | n_train | n_test |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.6261 | 0.8732 | 3,885 | 972 |

Overall weighted accuracy (0.8730) is high but driven almost entirely by the None and Low classes, which together make up 95.7% of the data. Macro-F1 (0.6247) — which weights all four label classes equally regardless of size — is the more honest summary and is substantially lower, dragged down entirely by the High row.

### 4.4 The zero "High" examples limitation

**Model 2 has never seen a single "High" example, in training or in test, across all 5 folds — and cannot, given how its target label is currently constructed.**

The AI-integration level is not an independently assessed label. It is *derived* from the relevance label plus an "intensity" score (0–3) via a fixed rule (`derive_ai_integration_level()` in `src/train_ai_integration_model.py`):

- Exclude or Company-context only → **None**
- Adjacent → **Low** if intensity ≤ 1, else **Moderate**
- Core → **Moderate** if intensity ≤ 1, else **High**

The intensity field this rule depends on (`agent_loop_clean_intensity`) is **0 for all 4,857 rows** in the current dataset — verified directly against the training file. This is not noise or a labeling gap; it is a structural placeholder. The upstream cleaning step (`src/05_clean_agent_loop_labels.py`) explicitly falls back to a hardcoded intensity of "0" for every row because no intensity field exists yet in this labeling schema (the agent loop currently outputs Core/Adjacent/Company-context only/Exclude + role + confidence, but no 0–3 intensity score). Since intensity is always 0 (≤ 1), the derivation rule can only ever produce None, Low, or Moderate — **High is mathematically unreachable under the current label schema**, regardless of how well any model performs.

A direct consequence, also worth stating plainly: because intensity is constant, the AI-integration target is presently a **deterministic recoding of Model 1's relevance label** — Exclude/Company-context-only → None, Adjacent → Low, Core → Moderate, with no independent variation. Model 2's ~0.87 accuracy is therefore better read as "how well can a differently-featurized text classifier recover Model 1's relevance label, collapsed into three buckets" rather than as evidence of predicting a genuinely distinct "AI intensity" construct. This is also documented directly in the serving code (`backend/app.py`): "there were zero 'High' examples in the training data, so this model can never return 'High' even though the label schema defines it." Adding a populated 0–3 intensity field to the labeling schema is a prerequisite for Model 2 to become a non-trivial addition to Model 1, and for "High" to become reachable at all.

## 5. What drives predictions — interpretability / sanity check

Source: `outputs/model2_ai_integration_logreg_coefficients.csv` (top 20 positive and negative TF-IDF-term coefficients per class, from the final logistic regression model fit on all 4,857 postings).

The coefficient patterns line up with domain intuition, which is a useful sanity check that the model is picking up genuine signal rather than spurious correlations:

**None** (business/commercial roles, no AI integration): top positive terms are **sales** (+2.457), **business** (+2.043), **finance** (+1.513), **manager** (+1.422), **marketing** (+1.376), **accounting** (+1.221), **financial** (+1.163) — squarely commercial/administrative vocabulary. Top negative terms (push *away* from None) are **lab** (−1.739), **laboratory** (−1.512), **quality** (−1.415), **scientific** (−1.400), **scientist** (−1.379), **study** (−1.345), **regulatory** (−1.304) — technical/scientific vocabulary.

**Low** (wet-lab/manufacturing-adjacent, minimal AI/data): top positive terms are **laboratory** (+2.213), **lab** (+1.956), **manufacturing** (+1.873), **regulatory** (+1.493), **scientific** (+1.482), **engineering** (+1.466), **scientist** (+1.461), **cgmp** (+1.236) — bench-science and GMP-manufacturing vocabulary. Top negative terms are **sales** (−1.738), **manager** (−1.358), **data management** (−1.320), **statistical** (−1.278), **business** (−1.269), **finance** (−1.102), **sas** (−1.068) — commercial and data-science vocabulary pulling *away* from Low.

**Moderate** (data/statistical-programming roles): top positive terms are **data** (+1.973), **data management** (+1.927), **statistical** (+1.846), **programming** (+1.789), **sas** (+1.660), **datasets** (+1.560), **proteomics** (+1.155), **biostatistics** (+1.110), **cdisc** (+1.040), **sdtm** (+0.901) — data science/biostatistics/clinical-data vocabulary, exactly the profile expected for genuine data/AI-adjacent work. Top negative terms are **able** (−0.849), **manufacturing** (−0.847), **equipment** (−0.828), **business** (−0.789), **sales** (−0.720), **laboratory** (−0.701) — wet-lab and commercial vocabulary pulling away.

Summary pattern requested for sanity-checking: **sales/finance → None**, **lab/manufacturing → Low**, **data/statistical/SAS → Moderate** — all three hold up directly in the coefficient rankings above. This indicates the model has learned a coherent, domain-plausible signal rather than an arbitrary one, even though (per §4.4) its target label is a deterministic recoding of Model 1's relevance label.

---

## 6. Known limitations

1. **Labeling completeness:** the full 4,857-posting candidate pool is labeled (4,857 of 4,857) — this is not a partial sample. However, the pool itself is a rule-filtered subset of a much larger raw archive (123,849 postings), and labels come from an AI agent loop with rule-based QC, not independent human adjudication. The QC correction step ran but changed 0 labels on this dataset (§2.1).
2. **No held-out test set beyond cross-validation.** All reported metrics (both models) come from 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the same 4,857-posting set used to fit the final deployed models. There is no separate, never-touched holdout or out-of-time test set. Performance on genuinely new postings (different time period, different source, different phrasing conventions) is untested.
3. **Single-label classification.** Each posting receives exactly one relevance label and one AI-integration level. Postings with genuinely overlapping characteristics (e.g., a role that is both technical and commercial) are forced into a single bucket, which is a source of some of the confusion-matrix overlap seen in §3.2 and §4.2.
4. **The AI-integration target is currently a deterministic function of the relevance label** (§4.4), not an independently observed construct, because the intensity field is uniformly 0. "High" is unreachable, and Model 2's apparent accuracy partly reflects recovering a recoded version of Model 1's own label using a different feature representation, not validated evidence of measuring AI-integration intensity per se.
5. **Sample-size caveats on smaller classes.** Core (210 postings, 4.3% of the data) and, by construction, Moderate (also 210, since Moderate = Core) are both small relative to the other classes. Their F1-scores (0.6502 for Core in Model 1; 0.7419 for Moderate in Model 2) are based on far fewer examples than None/Low/Adjacent/Company-context-only/Exclude and should be read with wider uncertainty — a handful of additional or removed examples could shift these numbers more than it would shift the majority-class scores.
6. **Confidence scores are coarse.** The AI labeling agent's self-reported confidence takes essentially two values across the entire dataset (0.70 or 0.85), suggesting a template-level rather than per-posting confidence estimate — it should not be treated as a calibrated per-example reliability signal.
7. **Gate leakage (Model 1 → Model 2 pipeline effect):** because Model 1 is not perfectly precise/recall-balanced on Exclude (§3.4), roughly 1 in 5 truly out-of-scope postings will still reach Model 2 and receive a (spurious) AI-integration score in the deployed two-stage pipeline, and roughly 1 in 5 postings the gate calls Exclude are actually relevant and get rejected before ever reaching Model 2.
